product: SmartCiti.X : Trade Craft Academy (powered by AGI Corp)

honesty.textures: no texture, photograph or artwork file exists in this repository and none is downloaded: every surface is a recipe - a base colour, a grain, an octave count and a relief depth - and the page generates the image and its normal map in the learner's own browser at boot. There is therefore no third-party artwork anywhere in the render.
honesty.weather: schematic weather, not a forecast and not an observation: nothing here is tied to a reading taken at any real place or time, and the per-campus atmospheres are authored by reputation rather than measured.
honesty.fauna: ambience, not a wildlife survey: common names, schematic bodies and authored paths. No species record, population count or sighting is claimed, and no animal here is drawn from any photograph.
honesty.sky: the sky is generated, not photographed, and the night sky is placed by a fixed seed rather than from any star catalogue - it is a night sky, not the night sky.
honesty.ground: the ground a campus stands on is SCHEMATIC like the buildings on it: the surfaces are the ones the trade actually works over, but their extent and placement are drawn to teach, not surveyed.
honesty.recipes: every ground recipe is AUTHORED, and authored the way the campus atmospheres and the built fabric are: composed from the character a place is known for - shell fill in a delta, slag in a mill valley, limerock on a subtropical coast - and never taken from a survey, a photograph or a scan of any real yard. What a place is built on is a reputation, and this record says so rather than implying someone went and looked.

sky.projection: equirectangular, drawn to a 1024x512 canvas at boot

disc.placement: the disc is drawn where the key light actually comes from - its azimuth and elevation are read off the light, so the sun in the sky and the shadows on the ground agree rather than merely coexisting

horizon_haze.note: a bright band just above the horizon so the dome does not end on a hard edge; a campus that names its own haze overrides day_tint

stars.note: placed by a fixed seed, so the sky is the same sky every time the page is opened - no two learners see a different night

clouds.note: value noise, thickened or thinned by the weather record rather than by a separate cloud asset

clear.name: Clear
clear.blurb: the working day the halls were drawn for - hard shadows, dry ground, and nothing in the air to hide a hand signal

overcast.name: Overcast
overcast.blurb: flat light, no shadows to judge a line by - the light a layout hand complains about

fog.name: Fog
fog.blurb: the visibility a crane signal has to survive; the Bay campuses were drawn with this in mind, and it leaves the ground damp without a drop having fallen

rain.name: Rain
rain.blurb: wet ground, longer stopping distances, and every surface in the yard reading differently

storm.name: Storm
storm.blurb: the condition that stops a lift - and the one worth practising the stop in

night.name: Night
night.blurb: the shift most of this work actually happens on - dew on the steel by the small hours, and every edge lit by a tower rather than by the sun

asphalt.name: Asphalt
asphalt.where: the yard running surface and the ring road
asphalt.why: a binder course that has been driven on goes grey in the wheel tracks and keeps its aggregate proud everywhere else, so it wants fine octaves rather than a flat black

concrete.name: Concrete
concrete.why: a power-trowelled slab is nearly flat and still not smooth: the relief is small on purpose and the grain does the work

gravel.name: Compacted gravel
gravel.where: the plant yard, where the machines actually track
gravel.why: loose aggregate is all edge and shadow; it is the deepest relief in the table short of ballast, because that is what it looks like from a metre up

grass.name: Rough grass
grass.where: the campus green and the verges
grass.why: unirrigated mown grass is never one green: the extra octave is the mower pattern and the dry patches it leaves

sand.name: Sand and fill
sand.why: a cut face and a stockpile are the same material at two angles of repose, so it is graded fine and lit soft

marsh.name: Tidal marsh
marsh.where: vegetated tidal marsh, wet underfoot between the channels
marsh.why: pickleweed and cordgrass stand in clumps with water between them, which is a clumped grain and a trace of sheen

mudflat.name: Tidal flat
mudflat.where: the intertidal flat a managed pond becomes as it reopens
mudflat.why: a flat that has just drained holds a film of water in every channel, so it is the least rough ground in the table that is not open water

upland.name: Dry upland
upland.where: the dry ground above the tide line and on made land: where the uplands are planted back, and the windward fill of an island yard that nobody waters
upland.why: dry grass over a thin soil shows the ground through it, which is a bright grain on a drab base rather than a green

levee.name: Levee crown
levee.where: the compacted crown of a dike or levee, which is the path a crew actually walks a diked site on
levee.why: a crown is rutted along its length by the truck that maintains it and loose at the edges where nothing drives

water.name: Open water
water.where: the Bay, the estuary and the river
water.why: the only surface here that is more mirror than material, which is what the low roughness and high metalness say

salt-slab.name: Salt-weathered slab
salt-slab.where: the concrete apron of a former naval station on made ground, bleached pale and stained at every joint
salt-slab.why: salt air takes the fines out of a slab and leaves the aggregate standing: it is paler, pitted and rust-flecked where the reinforcement is closest to the top

hardstand.name: Container hardstand
hardstand.where: the crane-rated hardstand of a working terminal, rutted on the turning circles and patched everywhere else
hardstand.why: a surface built to carry a loaded stacker is repaired in pieces for thirty years, so it reads as patchwork - the coarse octaves are the patches, not noise

shell.name: Crushed shell
shell.where: the crushed-shell yard fill of a delta with no rock in it, pale, sharp and loud underfoot
shell.why: the Gulf delta has shell where other places have quarry stone, and a shell yard is far brighter than the ground beside it - which is the whole look of the place

caliche.name: Caliche pad
caliche.where: the caliche and crushed-limestone pad a coastal-plain plant yard is built up on, above ground that moves
caliche.why: gumbo clay swells and shrinks with every wet season, so the yard is a pad brought in on trucks: buff, dusty dry and set hard, with nothing of the soil under it showing

ballast.name: Track ballast
ballast.where: the angular crushed stone of a rail yard, laid to drain and never laid to be walked on
ballast.why: ballast is deliberately sharp and deliberately loose so it keys together and sheds water; it is the deepest relief in the table because every stone casts on its neighbour

basalt.name: Crushed basalt
basalt.where: the blue-grey crushed basalt a rain-country yard is surfaced with, darker in the joints where it stays wet
basalt.why: the Cascade quarries are basalt, and in a climate that never fully dries the stone reads blue-grey and the gaps between it read green

slag.name: Air-cooled slag
slag.where: the pale vesicular slag a mill valley paved its own yards and roadbeds with, for a century, because it had it
slag.why: air-cooled blast-furnace slag is light, sharp and full of holes: it is paler than the stone around it and it glints, which is why the metalness is not quite zero

decomposed-granite.name: Decomposed granite
decomposed-granite.where: the granitic fines and road base of a Front Range yard, pale gold and raising dust in a dry month
decomposed-granite.why: granite weathering in a dry climate leaves a compacted sandy fine that packs like paving and travels like dust, which is a low relief over a high speckle

limerock.name: Crushed limerock
limerock.where: the crushed oolitic limestone a subtropical coast quarries out from under itself and lays everything on
limerock.why: South Florida builds on the rock it is standing on, and that rock is near-white: it is the brightest ground in the table, and under a high sun it is the reason for sunglasses

cinder.name: Cinder and clinker
cinder.where: the black cinder and clinker fill a coal-era plant yard was raised on and never took back up
cinder.why: boiler ash went under the yard because it was free and it drained; a century later it is still what the ground is, dark and rust-flecked with what the shops dropped on it

prairie.name: Prairie grass
prairie.where: the unmown bunch grass of a plains or coastal-prairie verge, gold more of the year than it is green
prairie.why: prairie grass grows in clumps with bare ground between them and cures standing, so the base is straw and the grain is straw - a green verge would be the wrong country

moss.name: Moss and wet turf
moss.where: the shaded rain-fed verge of a temperate-rainforest yard, which takes the joints of the path as well
moss.why: in a place that is wet nine months of the year moss is the ground cover rather than a defect in it: deeper green than grass, softer relief, and never quite matte

ground_laid_elsewhere.asphalt: the page's own made land and the fallback carriageway
ground_laid_elsewhere.concrete: the page's slabs, walkways and building aprons
ground_laid_elsewhere.sand: the page's stockpiles and the excavator cut, and the sandy habitat of a restoration site
ground_laid_elsewhere.water: the page's open water, at every campus that has any
ground_laid_elsewhere.mudflat: a Bay Restoration site whose habitat line is tidal flat
ground_laid_elsewhere.levee: a Bay Restoration site walked along its dike crown

gull.name: Gull
gull.why: a working waterfront has gulls over it; both Bay campuses and the Sound waterfront at Seattle are on one

pelican.name: Brown pelican
pelican.why: Louisiana’s state bird, and unmistakable over any Gulf coast or Biscayne Bay alike - the ship channel and the working port both

ring-billed-gull.name: Ring-billed gull
ring-billed-gull.why: the lakefront gull, by reputation the most familiar bird on the Chicago waterfront

egret.name: Egret
egret.why: standing in the wet margin, which is most of the ground around this campus

pigeon.name: Pigeon
pigeon.why: every yard in every city has them, and they are the scale reference nobody thinks about

yard-dog.name: Yard dog
yard-dog.why: the yard dog is a fixture of the trade, and it teaches the habit of looking down before reversing

treasure-island.ground_why: a former naval station on made ground: the yard is the station's own apron, and a lifetime of salt air has taken the face off it. The verge is the dry, windswept fill nobody waters - an island lawn would be somebody else's campus
treasure-island.character: marine layer off the Pacific; cool, grey and bright at once, and the thickest air on the network - authored by reputation, not measured

oakland.ground_why: a working container terminal on the estuary: the yard is crane-rated hardstand, patched in pieces where the stackers turn, and the verge is the gravel margin every truck parks half on
oakland.character: the estuary side, warmer and harder-edged than the island, with one thin bank off the water that is gone by the time the yard is working - authored by reputation, not measured

new-orleans.ground_why: a delta with no rock in it fills its yards with crushed shell, and this campus sits between the river and the wet margin the egret is standing in - so the verge is marsh, which is what the animal record has always said the ground here was
new-orleans.character: Gulf humidity and a low warm haze that does not lift with the morning, and river fog off the water before it - authored by reputation, not measured

houston.ground_why: a ship-channel plant yard standing on gumbo clay is a caliche pad brought in above ground that moves with every wet season, and what is left unpaved goes back to Gulf coastal prairie rather than lawn
houston.character: Gulf-coast heat haze over a working ship channel that never clears the way a sea breeze clears, and a refinery glow at the sky's edge after dark - authored by reputation, not measured

chicago.ground_why: a rail hub is laid on the same crushed stone as the track running through it, sharp and loose and laid to drain, and the verge is the tallgrass prairie holding the embankment either side of it
chicago.character: a flat lakefront wind that never really stops, cold and grey off the water most of the year - authored by reputation, not measured

seattle.ground_why: Cascade basalt is the aggregate at hand here, and in a climate this wet the verge is not grass but moss - in the shade of the yard, and then in the joints of its paths
seattle.character: a low marine overcast off the Sound that sits on the cranes rather than above them, a working waterfront and the hum of aerospace manufacturing just south of the green - authored by reputation, not measured

pittsburgh.ground_why: a mill valley paved its own yards and roadbeds with the slag its furnaces made, because it had it by the trainload; the verge is the rough grass of the hillside the shop is cut into
pittsburgh.character: a river haze that settles in the valley overnight and burns off late, over three confluent rivers crossed by more bridges than any other American city, and a post-industrial skyline standing where the mills once were - authored by reputation, not measured

denver.ground_why: Front Range granite weathers to a fine that compacts like paving and travels like dust, which is what a high dry yard is surfaced with; the verge is shortgrass, gold for most of the year, because nothing else survives a mile up without water
denver.character: thin, dry high-altitude light off the Front Range with a view that goes as far as the ground allows, a mining and energy heritage at 5,280 feet, and the Rockies standing on the western horizon - authored by reputation, not measured

miami.ground_why: everything in South Florida is laid on the limerock quarried out from under it, and it is near-white under a high sun; the verge is the coarse turf that survives salt, heat and a rainy season
miami.character: subtropical coastal heat and humidity off Biscayne Bay, afternoon thunderheads stacking through hurricane season, and a working seaport at the harbor's edge - authored by reputation, not measured

detroit.ground_why: a coal-era plant yard was raised on its own boiler ash because the ash was free and it drained, and nobody has ever taken it back up; the verge is the gravel margin between the shops and the rail spur
detroit.character: a Great Lakes river haze off the Detroit River, a working industrial waterfront across from Windsor, Ontario, and a century of automotive manufacturing standing behind the skyline - authored by reputation, not measured

treasure-island.why: the flat-roofed concrete and steel sheds of a former naval station, pale and salt-weathered

oakland.why: estuary-side brick warehousing under sawtooth light monitors, warmer and harder-edged than the island

new-orleans.why: stuccoed masonry under pitched roofs with deep galleries, built for rain and shade

houston.why: metal-clad process plant at petrochemical scale, flat and wide with everything on the outside

chicago.why: load-bearing masonry on a steel frame behind a flat parapet, the city that invented the arrangement

seattle.why: heavy timber and glass under a pitched roof, green-grey and built to shed rain

pittsburgh.why: mill brick and blackened structural steel under sawtooth glazing, a river valley of shops

denver.why: concrete block and stone in high-desert buff, flat-roofed under a dry sky

miami.why: light stucco with shuttered openings and flat roofs, detailed for wind and sun

detroit.why: heavy plant in block and steel under sawtooth bays, built around the line rather than the street
